extracted.intended_audience: NSF proposers (PIs), peer reviewers, and NSF program staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on NSF's merit review principles and criteria for evaluating grant proposals, plus requirements for special proposal mechanisms (accomplishment-based renewals and creativity extensions) and expectations for assessment, documentation, and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle: Highest quality and potential to advance knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: All NSF projects should be of the highest quality and have the potential to advance, if not transform, the frontiers of knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle: Contribution to broader societal goals (Broader Impacts)
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF projects, in the aggregate, should contribute more broadly to achieving societal goals. These broader impacts may be accomplished through the research itself, through activities that are directly related to specific research projects, or through activities that are supported by, but are complementary to, the project. The project activities may be based on previously established and/or innovative methods and approaches, but in either case must be well justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broader impacts can be achieved via research or complementary activities; proposals should justify the chosen approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle: Meaningful assessment and appropriate evaluation metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Meaningful assessment and evaluation of NSF funded projects should be based on appropriate metrics, keeping in mind the likely correlation between the effect of broader impacts and the resources provided to implement projects. If the size of the activity is limited, evaluation of that activity in isolation is not likely to be meaningful. Thus, assessing the effectiveness of these activities may best be done at a higher, more aggregated, level than the individual project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIs are expected to be accountable for carrying out activities described in the funded project. Individual projects should include clearly stated goals, specific descriptions of the activities that the PI intends to do, and a plan in place to document the outputs of those activities. Small-scale activities may require aggregated evaluation across projects to assess effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of two National Science Board–approved merit review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: All NSF proposals are evaluated through the use of two National Science Board-approved merit review criteria. Both criteria are to be given full consideration during the review and decision-making processes; each criterion is necessary but neither, by itself, is sufficient. Therefore, proposers must fully address both criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In some instances, NSF will employ additional criteria as required to highlight specific program objectives. Reviewers are strongly encouraged to familiarize themselves with the criteria, including PAPPG Chapter II.C.2.d.(i), prior to reviewing a proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accomplishment-based renewal proposal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In an accomplishment-based renewal, the project description is replaced by copies of no more than six reprints of publications resulting from the research supported by NSF (or research supported by other sources that is closely related to the NSF-supported research) during the preceding three- to five-year period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An accomplishment-based renewal must also include a brief (not to exceed four pages) summary of plans for the proposed support period and information on human resources development at the post-doctoral, graduate, and undergraduate levels. All other information required for NSF proposal submission remains the same. Proposals undergo merit review in the tradition of the specific program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creativity Extension eligibility and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: A program officer may recommend the extension of funding for certain research grants beyond the initial period for which the grant was awarded, for a period of up to two years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The objective of such extensions is to offer the most creative investigators an extended opportunity to attack adventurous, 'high-risk' opportunities in the same general research area, but not necessarily covered by the original/current award. Awards eligible for such an extension are generally three-year continuing grants. Special Creativity Extensions are normally initiated by the NSF program officer based on progress during the first two years of the grant.
